unresolvedWorkerFailures.reason: Worker worklog-draft requires review or hardware/account input: Feature 35 slice. New pure module src/ui/worklog-draft.ts exports buildWorklogDraft(input, {since, until, capsuleId?, format, now?}). Input is {checkpoints, tasks, notes, focusSessions} using the existing field names (Checkpoint.createdAt/capsuleId/refs, Task.done/createdAt with optional completedAt/updatedAt, Note.updatedAt, FocusSession.endedAt/outcome/capsuleId/taskId). The window is half-open: since <= t < until. Records are grouped into Done (checkpoints, done tasks, completed focus), In progress (updated notes, focus stopped early) and Blocked/Open (open tasks). Each bullet carries {kind,id,title} evidence and a [kind:id] tag in the text. Sorting is deterministic. Markdown output differs by format (standup or worklog). With capsuleId, only that project's checkpoints and focus sessions are kept, plus the tasks and notes they reference. When nothing matches it returns {text:'',sections:[],evidence:[],empty:true}. It throws descriptive Errors for non-ISO or invalid dates, since >= until, since in the future, and a bad format. No network and no model. MemoryWorkbench.tsx: one import, the recap section now also renders a new StandupDraft panel (window select today/24h/7d, project select, Standup/Worklog Segmented toggle, a 'Draft standup' button, a read-only textarea, a 'Copy draft' button that uses navigator.clipboard when present, and an empty-state message). Existing sections, shortcuts and reduced-motion handling are unchanged. Added tests/slice-worklog-draft.test.mjs with 7 tests (esbuild data-URL import) covering window boundaries, grouping, evidence per bullet, capsule filter, determinism under reordering, empty result and invalid-window rejection.

Worker error-diagnosis requires review or hardware/account input: Feature 28 slice: new pure module src/ui/error-diagnosis.ts exports diagnoseErrorText(text) (plus extractPaths, DIAGNOSIS_LIMITS, NO_PATTERN_TEXT). Offline rules only, no model call, no file access, no execution. Detects ENOENT, EACCES, EPERM, EADDRINUSE (with port), ECONNREFUSED (with address), Cannot find module, JavaScript heap out of memory, Windows HRESULT 0x8xxxxxxx (known codes high confidence, unknown low), 'Access is denied', Python Traceback and ModuleNotFoundError, and 'port N already in use'. Extracts Windows/POSIX paths (including paths with spaces inside stack-frame parentheses, quotes and Python File "...", line N) and line:col locations as plain strings; input capped at 20000 chars with truncated flag. Proposed actions (open-path, reveal-folder, copy-text, open-settings) are previews with requiresConfirmation:true and exact targets, never shell commands; unknown input yields matches:[], one copy-text action and the summary 'No known pattern recognized...'. PromptTools.tsx gets a 'Diagnose error' panel (textarea, Diagnose button, results with title/explanation/confidence, locations, 'Proposed actions (preview)'). copy-text uses the panel's existing clipboard copy helper on explicit click; open-path, reveal-folder and open-settings have no existing bridge (ActionRequest has no open-path/reveal type), so they render as disabled 'Not available in this build'. New tests/slice-error-diagnosis.test.mjs (esbuild data-URL bundling) covers every pattern family, Windows stack-trace path extraction, truncation, unknown input and action safety.

Worker clip-export requires review or hardware/account input: Feature 140 slice. New pure module src/ui/clip-export.ts exports sampleClip(sceneOrLab, {fps, durationMs, reducedMotion?}), parseClip(json), clipToBlobParts(clip), plus clipExportFrameCount, clipByteSize and formatBytes. It reuses labFromScene/resolveLayer/layerRate from motion-presets and framePhase/round from motion-timing, so per-frame, per-layer values (x, y, opacity, scale, phase, hue) are deterministic and computed without the DOM or requestAnimationFrame. fps must be an integer from 1 to 60 and durationMs must be 100..30000; values outside those ranges throw descriptive Errors. frameCount = max(1, round(fps*durationMs/1000)). Output uses the envelope {format:'desktop-companion-clip', version:1, sceneId, fps, durationMs, frameCount, reducedMotion, frames:[{t(ms), elements}], license:'original'}. With reduced motion, every frame holds the poster frame. parseClip checks size, JSON, format, version, license, sceneId, fps and duration bounds, that frameCount matches fps and duration, frame count, strictly increasing t, element ids, kinds and finite numbers, and opacity range. It drops unknown keys. MotionStudio.tsx adds an Export clip group to the Clip export panel with a 12/24/30/60 fps select and a bounded ms duration input. 'Export clip' samples the current lab, shows frameCount and estimated size, and then a 'Download clip JSON' button downloads it through the existing downloadBlob (URL.createObjectURL plus revoke). The prepared clip is invalidated when the lab, fps, duration or reduced-motion setting changes, and the component's reducedMotion prop is passed through. Small .motion-clip-json and .motion-clip-summary styles were added. The new tests/slice-clip-export.test.mjs uses the esbuild data-URL pattern and covers purity, the frameCount formula, monotonic times, determinism, reduced-motion stills, bounds rejection, a parseClip round-trip, and rejection of a tampered frameCount, wrong format, version, license, fps, non-increasing times and an unknown kind. It also checks the MotionStudio wiring.
